title: Mirai Worm Investigation
description: Investigate an infection of the Mirai worm within a controlled network environment. Identify the extent of the infection, understand the propagation mechanism, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Mirai worm is a well-known malware that targets Linux systems, particularly IoT devices. It propagates by exploiting vulnerabilities and uses compromised devices to launch distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. In this scenario, you will investigate an infection of the Mirai worm within a controlled network environment. Your goal is to identify the extent of the infection, understand the propagation mechanism, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `patient-zero` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this host, you can investigate the infection and access other compromised hosts within the network.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `patient-zero` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From this host, you can investigate the infection and access other compromised hosts within the network.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious scheduled task/timer used by the malware for persistence
levels.content: The Mirai worm uses a scheduled task to maintain persistence on infected hosts. Investigate the systemd timers on the `patient-zero` host to identify the malicious timer. The flag is the name of the timer.
levels.solution: The malicious timer used by the Mirai worm for persistence is `sysnet-monitor.timer`. This timer is located in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for timers in the `/etc/systemd/system/` directory.

levels.title: Identify the hidden malware directory used by the worm
levels.content: The Mirai worm creates a hidden directory to store its files. Investigate the file system on the `patient-zero` host to locate this directory. The flag is the path to the hidden directory.
levels.solution: The hidden malware directory used by the Mirai worm is `/opt/.worm`. This directory contains the worm's files and logs.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check directories in `/opt/` for suspicious names.

levels.title: Identify the compromised host discovered through propagation logs
levels.content: The Mirai worm logs its propagation activities. Investigate the spread log on the `patient-zero` host to identify a compromised host. The flag is the IP address of the compromised host.
levels.solution: The compromised host discovered through propagation logs is `192.168.90.10`. This host was compromised by the Mirai worm and is part of the infected network.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the spread log located in the hidden malware directory.
